reference.title: Cora Pike
reference.summary: A Blackbriar clerk whose loyalty breaks when Judith's custody system consumes her own household.
reference.content: Cora knows the hall's store records, staff routines, and ordinary relief work. Her authored record describes her starting position; her defection remains play history in the journal.

links.context: Present among Judith's dependents before her break with the household regime.
Knows the stores, staff, and custody records; this is the most likely point of defection.
Her family evidence connects the Pike dead to Mercy House transfers.
Her household connections help identify names and vessels moved through the mirror route.

runtime_evidence.observed_change: Cora joins the commission with six defecting staff and later protects relief stores.
runtime_evidence.contract_effect: No authored reference mutation and no new runtime event type.

reference.title: Blackbriar Hall and Grounds
reference.summary: Judith Crowl's estate, including its public hall, service wood, and ritual underhall.
reference.content: The estate record holds reusable approaches, ownership, staff circulation, and the relationship among the public house, covert service routes, and the chambers below.

links.context: The public administrative and relief-facing center of the estate.
The estate's service approaches, transfer wagons, and hidden route network.
The ritual complex beneath the hall and the estate's final convergence point.

reference.title: Saint Mercy House
reference.summary: A genuine relief institution converted into Judith's system of custody, leverage, and transfer.
reference.content: The organization record distinguishes the institution, its staff, dependents, records, routes, and legitimate care work from the encounter that occurs in its principal building.

links.context: Judith uses promised admission and dependent households to compel obedience.
Mara's case packets trace disappearances and coerced transfers into the institution.
The organization's principal site, staff, dependents, and hidden rooms.
The estate controls its stores, records, and administrative dependencies.
Transfer traffic and false accounts connect the institution to the burial system.
Name vessels move from the institution through Judith's mirror route.

reference.title: The Aulonite Bronze Seal
reference.summary: A portable instrument of royal authority whose custody, use, and public handling shape the flight from Aulon.
reference.content: The seal's canonical description and legal significance remain stable while its carrier, evidentiary value, and immediate risk vary by encounter.

links.context: Ianthe begins with the seal and decides whether authority or misdirection should travel openly.
The warrant requires the seal preserved, making its custody part of the gate dispute.
The escort may separate Ianthe from the seal to divide the search.
Preparation choices determine who carries or displays the seal on the mounted road.
The seal can authenticate orders, create witnesses, or expose the escort to pursuit.
Boat assignments may separate the seal from Ianthe, witnesses, or the armed escort.
Records and the seal can correct the false abduction signal only if their custody is credible.
The harbor court treats the seal as a separate claimant object with its own custody lane.

fixtures.contract_effect: The existing adventure remains legal without creating records for every official, animal group, survey pin, or institution named in encounter prose.
